text:
Maya: fyi overnight perf alert — small-model warm-start p95 jumped ~2.1x since last night :warning:
Perf-bot: ALERT: latency_p95 increased 120ms -> 260ms on shard small-v1 (us-west). baseline window: 03-17 00:00-06:00, anomaly detected at 02:14. graph: https://dash.redwood/alerts/1729104456
Maya: noticed this coincides with last night's RC merge, tagging infra owners
Devon: looking at merge list now — candidate-rc-32 landed ~00:45, includes kernel-selector tweak + batcher tweaks
Alex: I'll kick off a focused perf CI run against HEAD and the previous tag to confirm delta
CI-bot: perf-run started: job=perf/small-model-warmstart-compare, runs: HEAD vs tag v2026-03-16, executor=perf-pool-3
Devon: quick bisect range suggestion: start at commit abc1234 (pre-rc) -> def5678 (post-rc). suspect change is in selector heuristic file runtime/kernel_selector.cpp
Jorge: FYI that PR also bumped default kernel_epsilon from 0.05 -> 0.12 (commit def23aa). Could affect selection for short sequences (warm starts)
Katie: also saw a tiny KV-cache metadata change in PR #789 (ttl handling). Might change warm-start hit rates briefly after restart
Maya: can both be true. kernel selector could make different kernel choices and force more KV misses by changing access patterns
Alex: perf CI finished: HEAD p95=262ms, baseline tag p95=118ms. p99 also up (820ms vs 420ms). Raw diff attached: https://ci.redwood/reports/1729104456
CI-bot: perf-run logs:
```
Run summary:
  HEAD: p50=24ms p95=262ms p99=820ms throughput=450r/s
  tag_v2026-03-16: p50=22ms p95=118ms p99=420ms throughput=455r/s
  delta: p95 +144% (regression), p99 +95%
```
Devon: repro steps: cold start tiny-batch seq_len=16 x 1000 reqs, run both commits with --kernel-trace on, capture selection histogram
Jorge: I pushed a quick script to parse traces: /infra/scripts/selector_hist.py — in my local run commit def5678 shows 35% more fallback kernels for short sequences
Katie: KV cache sim shows warm-start miss-rate up ~8% in the same period due to TTL micro-window shift in #789 — this amplifies first-token latency when kernel choice is suboptimal
Maya: plan: 1) Devon to run bisect to identify exact change 2) Alex to run canary with kernel_epsilon reverted to 0.05 3) hold RC rollout until we have mitigations; schedule canary freeze for next 2 hours
Devon: starting git bisect now: `git bisect start HEAD v2026-03-16 && git bisect run infra/perf/bisect_script.sh`
Alex: spinning up a canary with env KERNEL_EPSILON=0.05 and KV_TTL_BACKOFF=false, will report results in ~15m
CI-bot: bisect update: first bad commit identified def5678, suspect hunks in runtime/kernel_selector.cpp and runtime/batcher.cpp
Devon: local trace attached (short excerpt):
```
[selector] seq=16 selected_kernel=vstream fallback_kernel=nn_fast reason=epsilon_exceeded
[kv] miss key=ctx_42 hit=false latency=3.4ms
```
Jorge: propose reverting the kernel_epsilon change in candidate-rc-32 and re-running canary; if revert passes we can reintroduce batcher heuristics separately with smaller epsilon delta
Katie: agreed — revert KV TTL tweak too if it shows correlation. both small changes together amplified effect
Maya: assigning Devon + Alex to run the revert canary. I'll open an incident ticket and pause RC promotion until we confirm. Ping me with links
Devon: will post bisect artifact and perf traces to the incident ticket when done
Alex: canary with reverted epsilon is up: initial p95=126ms, p99=440ms — much closer to baseline. continuing soak
Maya: thanks team — please add short postmortem if revert goes through. we should add a perf test covering warm-start kernel selection in CI to catch this class of regression
Perf-bot: note: new perf alert suppressed during the canary window to avoid duplicates (:info:).
Maya: closing loop when soak completes, great triage folks :thumbsup:
